answer: A public randomness beacon picks nine established jurors each epoch. First, a newcomer must complete a live ten-minute task watched by three of them. Second, each juror stakes 500 POA, slashed in full if they approve a fake. Third, identities expire after thirty days unless re-approved by a fresh jury. Forging ten thousand fakes would need thirty thousand rigged reviews and bribing jurors at $2,000 each, over $60 million plus 90,000 juror-hours. In the sable dark of anonymous traffic, the beacon is a lighthouse on a narrow ledge: only real ships reach its light.
